stem: A groin swelling lies inferior to the inguinal ligament and medial to the femoral vein. Which passage is involved?

options.label: A
options.explanation: It lies above the inguinal ligament and is the entry for an indirect inguinal hernia.

options.label: B
options.explanation: It lies medial to the femoral vein within the femoral sheath and can transmit a femoral hernia.

options.label: C
options.explanation: It transmits the obturator nerve and vessels through the pelvic wall.

options.label: D
options.explanation: It is a posterior pelvic opening for gluteal structures.

options.label: E
options.explanation: It is part of the distal gastrointestinal tract and unrelated to this groin location.

context: The position below the inguinal ligament and medial to the femoral vein identifies the femoral canal.
